thread:
maya: incident-bot just paged me for a sustained rise in throttle_events and queue_depth on inference-prod-us-east-1. Noticing customer error rates up ~6% on POST /v1/generate. paging oncall now?
incident-bot: ALERT: inference.throttle.events >= 50 for 5m (hosts: gpu-pool-us-east-1-*) — severity: critical. Link: https://grafana.example.com/d/ai/production-overview
kevin: i'm on it, joining call. quick summary of current state?
maya: logs show a spike in queued_requests and tokens/sec around 22:03 UTC. Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough — several hosts hit device memory pressure and threw backend 429s.
robert: i'm grabbing the paged handoff. maya — please dump a short query of the alerting rules and which hosts are affected.
maya: here's the prom query I used: `sum by (instance)(increase(inference_throttle_events_total[5m]))` returns host list. Also `avg_over_time(queue_depth[5m])` shows the queue sitting ~480 on gpu-pool-us-east-1-a.
kevin: observed token generation latency spike too. traceback in pods shows repeated OOM on model shard 3. suspect kernel selection fell back to slower path and memory ballooned.
robert: mitigation steps: 1) temporarily relax scale-down and trigger a manual scale up of 3 nodes into the dedicated pool, 2) increase per-host soft concurrency limit to reduce queue backlog, 3) route traffic to standby region if capacity stays tight.
sam: can we do a quick debounce on the throttle alert so it doesn't spam paging for the same incident? currently it's per-instance.
kevin: i'm performing manual scale-up now: `infractl scale --pool gpu-pool-us-east-1 --add 3 --reason "emergency throttle"`
incident-bot: Action executed: scale requested, 3 nodes pending. ETA 90s.
maya: while nodes come up, i'm changing the autoscale policy temporally to prefer tokens/sec scaling rather than queue depth to avoid reactive overshoot. also increasing the queue_depth alert threshold to 600 for now to avoid noise.
robert: please post the exact alert change so we have it in the thread. we will revert in the postmortem.
maya: alert change (temporary):
```
- alert: HighQueueDepth
  expr: avg_over_time(queue_depth[5m]) > 400
+ alert: HighQueueDepth
  expr: avg_over_time(queue_depth[5m]) > 600
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
```
kevin: scaled nodes are registering. host pressure reducing, queue depth dropping to ~220. 429s on the API decreasing.
sam: created a quick dashboard panel for per-model throttle rate + tokens/sec: `boards/eng-sre/capacity-pulse` — link: https://grafana.example.com/d/capacity-pulse. Adding annotations for the scale action.
robert: good. customer impact? are we seeing client-reported errors beyond internal 429s?
maya: error rates peaked for a handful of customers around 22:05 — highest affected model was rdx-7b — about 0.3% of total requests failed with 429. Notified CS to expect uptick.
kevin: confirm throttle events are below alerting threshold now. we should avoid reverting the queue alert change until we finish root cause and stability checks.
robert: agreed. next steps for post-incident:
- tune autoscaler to use a blended signal: tokens/sec + queue_depth with a 1m/5m lookback to reduce oscillation
- change alerting to dedupe per-customer bursters and add a suppress window for repeated instance-level pages (5m) to reduce noise
- add a dashboard that surfaces per-model kv-cache hit rate and quantization fallback events (these correlate with mem pressure)
- create a runbook section for oncall to follow for throttles (scale steps, safe concurrency bump, fallback routing)

sam: i'll own the dashboard and panels. i'll add the quantization/fallback metrics and an annotation option for scale events. ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4201
maya: i'll open a config RFC for the autoscale blended signal and propose threshold values. will include simulation results.
kevin: i'll follow up with infra to reduce node spin-up lag — we had ~90s which pushed us into throttling.
robert: for immediate alert tuning, two concrete changes: 1) move HighQueueDepth to severity: warning and 10m for firing; 2) add a grouping key to throttle_events alert: `group_by: deployment,model` so we page per-service not per-instance. make sure we also add a notification to #eng-sre-silent for lower-severity noise.
maya: done — pushed PR to alerts repo: https://github.com/redwood/alerts/pull/279 — includes the `for: 10m` and grouping change.
kevin: running a small smoke test by replaying a short burst in staging using the same model mix, will validate the blended autoscale response.
robert: nice. final note for oncall handoff: I'll be primary until 23:15 UTC then hand to maya. please be ready to escalate if we see a secondary spike.
maya: acknowledged. i'll monitor dashboards and the CS channel.
sam: added post-incident checklist to the ticket (owner assignments + ETA end of day).
robert: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a short postmortem and the final revert plan for temporary alert changes. :thumbsup:
